what: HP Inc. makes personal computers and printers. The printer business is the more profitable one, because customers keep buying ink and toner cartridges long after they buy the printer.
customers: Consumers, businesses and institutions buying laptops, desktops, printers and supplies in more than 170 countries.
money: laptops, desktops, workstations and gaming PCs
printers and, above all, ink and toner supplies
moat: An installed base of printers that consume its own cartridges, plus commercial PC relationships and service contracts with large organisations.
risks: Memory and component costs have risen sharply, squeezing PC margins
Printing volumes decline structurally as offices print less
Revenue has fallen about 4% a year over three years
Analyst targets imply the shares are roughly fairly valued
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 28% with a dividend yield above 4%
An ageing installed base of PCs is due for replacement
Buybacks shrink the share count every year
watch: Printing supplies revenue and PC unit demand and pricing.
